body.p: The Git Branch Manager view shows the local and remote branches for the current repository. By default, it opens to the right of the editing area. You can open it in any of the following ways:

ul.li: Click Show Git Branch Manager in the toolbar of the Git Staging view.
Go to Window Show View Git Branch Manager .

body.p: The view has the following areas:

ul.li: Text filter - Filters the branch tree.
Refresh - Reloads branch information for the current repository. Opening the view or clicking Refresh also fetches updates in the background so remote branches and tracking information stay current.
Repository tree - Shows the current repository and groups its branches into Local and Remote nodes.

section.title: Branch Tree
section.p: Use the branch tree to inspect local and remote branches. When you hover over a branch name, a tooltip shows information about the last commit on that branch, such as the author and commit date.
For remote branches, use Checkout branch to create a local branch from the selected remote branch.

The context menu for the remote branch area also provides fetch actions. Right-click Remote to fetch all configured remotes, or right-click an individual remote such as origin to fetch only that remote.

section.title: Local Branch Actions
section.p: Right-click a local branch to open its context menu. For a full list of available actions, see .
